wrapper_elaboration.observed: the whole 242-module design plus the wrapper elaborates with no warning

capability_findings.observed: The pinned ahb-lite plugin declares both vocabularies (13 CVW-named fields plus the 12 generic ids) and an x-role-alias-table mapping them, so an endpoint using the declaration's role names binds: this profile's 13 roles bound cleanly through P7-A.
The elaborated top exposes exactly the declaration's AHB-Lite roles; the manager-driven roles are outputs and the subordinate's completion is input.
PA_BITS=34 for XLEN=32, so the address port is two bits wider than the data ports; a contract that tied the address width to the data width would be wrong.
Read data arrives at the CPU boundary as HRDATAEXT; src/ebu/ebu.sv has no HRDATA port.

Elaborating the real module directly is impossible: verilator --lint-only --top-module wallypipelinedsoc over the full src tree exits 1 with 50 errors whose first is "Parameter without default value is never given value (IEEE 1800-2023 6.20.1): 'P'". The repository-authored typed top cvw_ahb_cpu_top includes the configuration headers and instantiates the SoC with #(P).
src/cvw.sv (the cvw package with the cvw_t typedef) must be compiled before the wrapper; with the wrapper first, Verilator fails with "Reference to 'cvw_t' before declaration".
rv32imc sets RESET_VECTOR = 64'h80000000; the boundary has no boot-address port.

unsupported.reason: configs/cpus/cvw/cvw_ahb_cpu_top.sv is verification code written in this repository; it is not part of git:2f2ddfd, so the source-lock verifier cannot authenticate its bytes against the pinned revision.
No local harness, adapter binding or generated artifact was produced for this boundary, and no AHB-Lite transaction has been run against the real RTL.

The wrapper does not export the integrated uncore's GPIO/UART/SPI/SDC/PWM pins, ExternalStall, TIMECLK or the internal reset output; it drives fixed values for the inputs. That is a wrapper-level environment choice, not an upstream fact.

runtime_renderer._AHB_LITE states the manager-driven roles as input while the bound endpoint carries the extractor's real directions (haddr/htrans/... output, hrdata/hready/hresp input); calling _shape(bound_endpoint, _AHB_LITE, []) refuses with 'runtime-endpoint-width-direction:cpu.external_bus:haddr'. Reconciling that frame is the remaining plumbing step before the AHB runtime branch could run.
